loc_todomvc.title: Lines of code (TodoMVC)
loc_todomvc.human: Fewer lines to read when someone else picks the project up.
loc_todomvc.method: Logic plus styles of a TodoMVC implementation, tests excluded. Counted by hand in the todomvc-compare repository.

deps_direct.title: Direct dependencies
deps_direct.human: Packages the framework itself declares. Every one of them is code you did not choose but still ship.
deps_direct.method: Sum of the `dependencies` fields of the packages installed by the framework's documented runtime install (react + react-dom, vue, svelte, solid-js). Frameworks with no documented bare npm runtime install are left blank.

deps_transitive.title: Packages installed
deps_transitive.human: How many separate packages end up in node_modules once npm is done resolving. Each one is a separate author you trust.
deps_transitive.method: `npm install --omit=dev` of the documented runtime packages into an empty project, then distinct name+version pairs in `npm ls --all --omit=dev`. Roots included.

node_modules_size.title: node_modules size
node_modules_size.human: Disk footprint of a clean install. It is not what ships to the browser, but it is what every CI run downloads.
node_modules_size.method: `du -sk node_modules` after `npm install --omit=dev` of the documented runtime packages into an empty project.

bundle_gzip.title: TodoMVC bundle, gzip
bundle_gzip.human: What the browser actually downloads for a small but complete application.
bundle_gzip.method: Gzipped production bundle of a TodoMVC implementation, measured in the todomvc-compare repository.

startup_bytes.title: Startup transfer
startup_bytes.human: Bytes pulled over the network before the benchmark application is usable. Same application in every column, so the difference is the framework.
startup_bytes.method: Lighthouse total byte weight for the js-framework-benchmark application, reported as benchmark 34_startup-totalbytes. Transfer size, not gzip specifically.

create_1k.title: Create 1,000 rows
create_1k.human: Time to put a thousand fresh rows on the screen. This is the wait after hitting a filter or opening a list.

update_1k.title: Partial update
update_1k.human: Touching every tenth row of a thousand, sixteen times. This is where a framework either finds the changed rows or re-checks everything.

swap_rows.title: Swap two rows
swap_rows.human: Two rows trade places out of a thousand. The ideal answer is two DOM moves, and the gap here shows who gets close to it.

remove_row.title: Remove one row
remove_row.human: Deleting a single row out of a thousand. The smallest possible change, so it measures the fixed cost of reacting at all.

mem_ready.title: Memory after load
mem_ready.human: Heap the framework occupies with nothing on the page yet.

mem_1k.title: Memory with 1,000 rows
mem_1k.human: Heap once a thousand rows are on screen. On a phone this is the difference between staying alive in the background and being killed.

startup_tbt.title: Startup blocking time
startup_tbt.human: How long the main thread is busy during startup, so taps and scrolls do nothing.
startup_tbt.method: js-framework-benchmark 32_startup-bt (Lighthouse total blocking time), arithmetic mean of 4 runs.

router.title: Router
router.human: Whether URLs and navigation come from the framework project itself, or you go pick a library and own that choice forever.
router.method: Yes when the framework project publishes and documents a routing solution of its own. No when its own official docs send you to a third-party project instead. Blank when neither is stated anywhere official.

i18n.title: Localization
i18n.human: Translating an application is rarely planned at the start and always arrives later.
i18n.method: Yes when the framework project publishes and documents localization support of its own.

themes.title: Theming
themes.human: Dark mode and brand colours without inventing your own CSS variable convention.
themes.method: Yes when the framework project publishes and documents a theming mechanism of its own.

virtual.title: List virtualization
virtual.human: Long lists stay smooth because off-screen rows are never rendered. Without it, someone eventually bolts a library onto a list that already shipped.
virtual.method: Yes when the framework project publishes and documents virtual scrolling of its own.

offline.title: Offline support
offline.human: A service worker set up by the framework rather than copied from a blog post.
offline.method: Yes when the framework project publishes and documents service worker support of its own.

ssr.title: Server rendering
ssr.human: Rendering to HTML on the server, for search engines and for the first paint.
ssr.method: Yes when the framework project publishes and documents a server rendering API of its own. No when its published module list contains no such module.

tests_nodom.title: Tests without a DOM
tests_nodom.human: Components testable as plain objects, with no browser and no jsdom to boot up first.
tests_nodom.method: Yes when components can be instantiated and asserted on outside a document, using the framework's own test runner.

di.title: Dependency injection
di.human: Swapping a real service for a fake one in a test without touching the component that uses it.
di.method: Yes when the framework project documents a dependency injection mechanism of its own.

forms.title: Forms
forms.human: Validation, dirty state and submission handled by the framework instead of a fourth form library per team.
forms.method: Yes when the framework project publishes and documents form handling of its own.

typed_templates.title: Typed templates
typed_templates.human: A typo in a template is caught by the compiler, not by a user.
typed_templates.method: Yes when the framework's official TypeScript documentation covers type checking of its template or view layer.

stars.title: GitHub stars
stars.human: A popularity signal, and nothing more. It says how many people bookmarked the repository, not how many shipped with it.
stars.method: `stargazers_count` from the GitHub API for the repository that holds the framework's current source.

npm_downloads.title: npm downloads
npm_downloads.human: The closest thing to a usage count. Inflated by CI runs, but inflated the same way for everyone.
npm_downloads.method: npm registry downloads for the last full week, for the package you install to use the framework.

so_questions.title: Stack Overflow questions
so_questions.human: How likely it is that your problem was already asked and answered by someone else.
so_questions.method: Question count of the framework's Stack Overflow tag, via the Stack Exchange API.

maintainers.title: npm maintainers
maintainers.human: How many people can publish a release. A low number is a bus factor.
maintainers.method: Length of the `maintainers` array in the npm registry metadata of the framework's primary package.

cve_tree.title: Known vulnerabilities
cve_tree.human: Advisories in the packages a clean install drags in. Someone has to triage each one of them.
cve_tree.method: `npm audit --omit=dev` on a fresh install of the documented runtime packages in an empty project.

breaking_3y.title: Breaking releases in 3 years
breaking_3y.human: Major versions shipped since 2023. Every one of them is a migration someone on the team pays for.
breaking_3y.method: Count of major semver versions of the framework's primary npm package first published in the last three years. Left blank for packages that do not use semver majors.
